Watching molecules move, atom by atom

children.label: Watching molecules move, atom by atom

children.value: Dirac’s “too complicated to be soluble” is no longer entirely true. Below, a water molecule vibrates in a simulation computed

: at every time step, the electrons’ Schrödinger equation is solved from scratch to obtain the forces on the nuclei. This technique, ab initio molecular dynamics, and its bigger sibling QM/MM (quantum region embedded in a classical environment, Nobel Prize 2013 to Karplus, Levitt, and Warshel) let chemists watch enzymes catalyze and materials fail, one femtosecond at a time.
狄拉克所说的“太复杂而无法求解”不再完全正确。下面展示了一个水分子在
的模拟中的振动：在每个时间步长，都从头求解电子的薛定谔方程以获得作用在原子核上的力。这种技术称为从头分子动力学，及其更强大的兄弟 QM/MM（量子区域嵌入经典环境，2013 年诺贝尔奖授予 Karplus、Levitt 和 Warshel），让化学家能够以飞秒为单位观察酶催化和材料失效的过程。

A quantum joke to start the semester
A police officer pulls Heisenberg over and asks, “Do you know how fast you were going?”
一名警察拦下海森堡，问道：“你知道你开多快吗？”
Heisenberg: “No, but I know exactly where I am.”
海森堡：“不知道，但我确切地知道我在哪里。”
The officer says, “You were doing 90 miles an hour!”
警官说：“你当时开到了 90 英里每小时！”
Heisenberg throws up his hands: “Great. Now I’m lost.”
海森堡无奈地摊开双手：“太好了。现在我迷路了。”
